rules: Choose CacheManager for process-local cached reads; choose SharedCacheManager for repeated eligible collection reads across trusted same-host workers. See getting-started/choose-a-manager.md.
Synchronous managers wrap pymongo.MongoClient and are imported from client_query_cache. Asyncio managers wrap pymongo.AsyncMongoClient and are imported from client_query_cache.asynchronous.

Rust-backed sharing reuses encoded documents and one stream per active database across workers. Process-local managers are independent. Sharing adds owner and miss costs; consult benchmarks/shared-cache.md before assuming speed or memory savings.
Check getting-started/installation.md#requirements for supported Python, PyMongo, operating system, shared-host capabilities and MongoDB prerequisites.

Create client_query_cache.CacheManager(client) or the asyncio equivalent for process-local caching. Reuse one manager per long-lived client per process; create both inside each worker, never before forking or per request.

Obtain a cached view with manager.get_cached_collection(collection) or manager[database][collection]. The collection must belong to that manager client; .raw preserves the original PyMongo collection and options.
Both managers provide find_one, find, aggregate, count_documents, estimated_document_count and distinct. Writes and administration use the original PyMongo collection or .raw.

Cached find() and aggregate() return native cursor subclasses. Materialize with list(cursor) or cursor.to_list() synchronously, or await cursor.to_list() with asyncio. Async find() returns immediately; await aggregate() to get its cursor.

Only complete successful cursor consumption can admit a bounded result. Close abandoned cursors. Started hit cursors keep an isolated snapshot through invalidation or closure; use a new execution for a new lookup.

Positive integer find limits can reuse complete results with larger positive or unlimited integer-zero/omitted limits when all other inputs match. Smaller sources cannot cover larger requests. Unlimited, negative and boolean requests use exact lookup.

Cached find() matches scalar-equality permutations in plain dicts: exact str fields not starting with $, and None or exact bool/int/float/str values. Other forms retain ordered matching and existing eligibility; native filters stay unchanged.

Use reference/api.md#single-document-reads for invalidation scope and reference/shared-cache.md#worker-managers-and-reads for shared eligibility. Never remove authorization predicates to obtain a cache hit.

Invalidation is asynchronous and has no per-write catch-up barrier or guaranteed delay. For read-after-write and current authorization, use direct PyMongo reads with suitable sessions and concerns. Direct reads do not refresh cached entries.

Eligible misses use primary, majority read concern even when unspecified. Secondary and non-majority read profiles bypass. Hits skip server execution and cannot reproduce fresh server errors or query effects.

Sessions, including session.bind(), bypass caching. Unsafe queries, views, time-series collections, missing collections, unsupported options and unavailable streams bypass; PyMongo operations can still fail.

Cursor-only find, $changeStream, Search/Vector Search, $text/$near/$nearSphere/$geoNear, $$USER_ROLES and nondeterministic reads bypass. Explicit find batching and aggregate batchSize at invocation bypass. See the API reference for precise query rules.
Configure CacheCoreConfig using reference/api.md#configuration and reference/api.md#limits. Consult operations/deployment.md#memory-beyond-the-cache-budget when sizing process memory.
The lag-window fields and validation rules are defined in reference/api.md#configuration; monitoring guidance is in operations/monitoring.md#observability.

Process-local snapshot(), stream_health_snapshot(name) and stream_cost_snapshot(name) do not start streams. Failed startup warns and retries on reads after cooldown, capped at 30 seconds. Established streams reconnect; healthy does not mean caught up.

Start SharedCacheServer once in the parent. Pass its private picklable connection to workers; each creates its own client and SharedCacheManager(client, connection). Never start a server in each FastAPI lifespan. See reference/shared-cache.md.

Run examples/fastapi_shared_example.py for FastAPI/Granian with actual spawned HTTP workers, cross-process hits, invalidation and graceful shutdown. Its reads retain a tenant predicate across workers.
Async SharedCacheManager requires async with or await SharedCacheManager.attach(client, connection). Construct and use it in one event loop.
Use reference/shared-cache.md#worker-managers-and-reads as the shared-read eligibility contract, including filter, projection, collation, codec and fallback rules.
Check operations/shared-cache.md#security-and-monitoring before distributing a SharedCacheConnection; it defines the worker trust boundary and database access requirements.
Configure SharedCacheConfig using reference/shared-cache.md#configuration. Collection-name and connection sizing guidance is in operations/shared-cache.md#collection-names-and-capacity.
Follow operations/shared-cache.md#collection-names-and-capacity for namespace sizing; drops release capacity and names beyond the configured limit bypass shared caching.
Use operations/monitoring.md#shared-manager-diagnostics for SharedCacheStatistics fields, scope and telemetry limitations; do not assume process-local diagnostics apply to shared managers.
Follow operations/shared-cache.md#consistency-and-recovery for owner outages and progress expiry, and reference/shared-cache.md#server-and-connection for cache_server.restart().

Close managers before caller-owned clients; await async close. Stop shared workers before closing the parent server. Never reuse clients, managers or servers inherited after fork; pass the connection. Async cleanup finishes before cancellation propagates.
Use operations/deployment.md#memory-beyond-the-cache-budget for process-local memory sizing and reference/shared-cache.md#configuration for shared capacity accounting.
